d.d: Initialism of abstract family of languages.
Often preceded by set: in or into flames; so as to be burned by fire.
In or into a colour like that of a flame.
In or into a state of great activity or emotion (anger, excitement, etc.).
With flames coming from it; burning, flaming, in flames, on fire.
Having the colour of a flame.
d.x: In autumn the trees are aflame with colour.

d.d: In a state of great activity or emotion (anger, excitement, etc.).
d.x: She said nothing and simply stared at him, eyes aflame.

d.d: Synonym of inflame (“to set (something) on fire; (figurative) to intensify or kindle (a feeling, such as appetite or passion); to intensify or kindle a feeling in (someone)”).
Chiefly in the present participle: to be in flames or on fire; to blaze, to flare up.
Any of a family of mycotoxins, produced by molds of the Aspergillus genus, that can be toxic, carcinogenic, mutagenic or teratogenic; typically found as contaminants of animal food or peanuts.
In or into a state of floating.
In, or while in, a vessel at sea or on another body of water; at sea.

d.x: A rubber duck and other toys were afloat in the bath.

d.d: In, or found while in, a vessel at sea or on another body of water.
Floating in the air; flowing freely; not tied, braided, etc. (of hair or clothing)
